Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Honolulu HI
341 PM HST Sat Jul 25 2026

.SYNOPSIS...
Breezy trade winds will usher in windward clouds and showers
through Monday. Hurricane Fausto is expected to weaken to a tropical
storm as it approaches the islands and will potentially bring
heavy rain, winds and surf to portions of the state Tuesday 
through Wednesday. Trades will fill in Thursday night in the wake 
of Fausto.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Breezy trade winds will usher in windward clouds and showers
through Monday. Incoming clouds and showers will focus over 
windward and mauka areas, mostly occurring during the nighttime
and early morning hours. 00Z soundings show a stable environment 
across the islands with an inversion around 8000 to 9000 feet.

The highlight next week will be the approach of now Hurricane
Fausto. Fausto is expected to weaken over the next several days as
it tracks west across higher shear and cooler waters, reaching 
the vicinity of the Hawaiian Islands on Tuesday. Main impacts
Tuesday and Wednesday include the possibility of strong winds, 
flooding rain and east shores surf, and will be dependent upon 
Fausto's eventual path. Winds could also be mitigated on a more 
northerly swing of the track, but more impactful if it slides 
southward, so confidence remains low. For rainfall, mitigating 
effects will be Fausto's relatively quick west movement limiting 
how long it will rain will last across each island, but our
terrain can capture much of this moisture as it passes through.
Meanwhile, swell generated by Fausto has the highest likelihood 
of occurrence, which will gradually build Sunday night through 
Monday night. 

No time like the present to review your family hurricane preparedness
plans, and ensure every household has at least a 14 day supply of
food and water available if needed during this years active hurricane
season.

A drier and more stable breezy trade wind pattern will fill in
across the state from Thursday onward as Fausto continues to 
journey westward away from the Hawaiian Islands. 


&&

.AVIATION...
Breezy trade winds will prevail through the rest of the weekend, 
before trending down on Sunday night. Afternoon satellite imagery 
and surface observations show some improvement in low clouds and 
showers across the western end of the state, but MVFR ceilings and
visibilities remain in place across windward sections of the 
central and eastern islands. Therefore, AIRMET Sierra remains in
effect for mountain obscuration for portions of the state. These 
showers and low clouds are expected to become less widespread
through early evening. AIRMET Tango also remains in effect for 
moderate low-level turbulence downwind of island terrain. This 
AIRMET will likely continue through at least Sunday.


&&

.MARINE...
Locally strong trades persist through Sunday then gradually back
to the NNE and diminish through midweek in response to TC Fausto 
passing north of the islands. The Small Craft Advisory for the 
windier waters of the Big Island and Maui County remains in effect
through tomorrow.

Plenty of long period energy observed upstream on offshore NDBC
buoy 51002 with several hours of moderate sized swell noted in 
the 16-19 second bands. Nearshore buoys indicate energy spread 
throughout the wave spectrum but most heavily concentrated in the 
long period bands in support of borderline High Surf Advisory 
(HSA) conditions for S facing shores this afternoon. The advisory 
remains in effect through tonight but may warrant an extension 
through Sunday conditional on overnight observations. 

Locally strong trades support rough surf along E shores slightly 
above the seasonal average through tonight. As trade wind swell 
declines with diminishing trades, a long period swell from 
Hurricane Fausto arrives tonight then builds through Sunday and 
Monday, peaking late Tuesday into Tuesday night. This swell is 
forecast to produce advisory-threshold surf along E facing shores 
as early as Sunday night followed by potential for warning-level 
surf as it peaks on Tuesday. After a brief lull mid-week, a medium
to long period E swell emanating from TC Genevieve in the E Pac 
will build Thursday night into the weekend.

Surf along N shores remains flat to tiny through the weekend. 
Some increase is expected as Fausto or its remnants pass over the 
region Tuesday and Wednesday.


&&
